faqs.question: How do I reset my university account password?
faqs.answer: Go to the self-service portal at accounts.northfield.edu and select 'Forgot Password'. Verify your identity with your registered mobile number or backup email, then choose a new password of at least 12 characters. If you are locked out and cannot verify, visit the IT Help Desk with a photo ID.

faqs.question: How do I connect to the campus Wi-Fi network?
faqs.answer: Select the 'NorthfieldSecure' network on your device and sign in with your university username and password. Install the security profile when prompted. Guests can use 'NorthfieldGuest', which requires a daily registration code from the visitor portal.

faqs.question: How do I set up the university VPN for off-campus access?
faqs.answer: Download the Northfield VPN client from software.northfield.edu, install it, and connect to vpn.northfield.edu using your university credentials and multi-factor approval. The VPN is required to reach library databases, research servers, and internal systems from outside campus.

faqs.question: How do I enroll in multi-factor authentication?
faqs.answer: Visit mfa.northfield.edu, sign in, and choose an authenticator app, a hardware security key, or SMS as your second factor. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app and enter the six-digit code to finish. Save your recovery codes in a safe place.

faqs.question: How can I access my student email account?
faqs.answer: Your student email is hosted on Microsoft 365. Sign in at outlook.northfield.edu with your full university email address (username@students.northfield.edu). You can also add the account to the Outlook or Mail app on your phone.

faqs.question: Where can I download free software like Microsoft Office?
faqs.answer: Enrolled students can download Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Cloud, MATLAB, and other licensed applications at software.northfield.edu. Sign in with your university account and follow the installation guide for your operating system. Licences remain active while you are enrolled.

faqs.question: How do I print or scan documents on campus?
faqs.answer: Use any PrintStation in the library or computing labs. Tap your student ID card, then release your job from the queue. Every student receives a quota of 500 pages per semester, and additional pages cost 5 cents each. Mobile printing is available through print.northfield.edu.

faqs.question: How do I report a phishing or suspicious email?
faqs.answer: Do not click links or open attachments. Use the 'Report Phish' button in Outlook, or forward the message as an attachment to security@northfield.edu. If you already entered your password, change it immediately and contact the IT Security team.

faqs.question: What are the IT Help Desk hours and how do I contact them?
faqs.answer: The IT Help Desk is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, and Saturday 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Reach us at helpdesk@northfield.edu, by phone at 555-0142, or through the live chat on the IT portal. The desk is located on the ground floor of the Main Library.

faqs.question: How can I access library databases and e-journals from home?
faqs.answer: Open library.northfield.edu, select a database, and sign in with your university account when prompted. If you are off campus and the database does not open, connect to the university VPN first. Librarians can help via chat during opening hours.

faqs.question: How do I apply for undergraduate admission?
faqs.answer: Complete the online application at admissions.northfield.edu, create an applicant account, fill in your academic history, write the personal statement, and pay the application fee. Once submitted, upload your supporting documents. You will receive a confirmation email with your applicant ID.

faqs.question: What are the application deadlines?
faqs.answer: Early Action applications close on November 1, Regular Decision applications close on January 15, and Spring Entry applications close on October 1. Financial aid forms and scholarship essays share the same deadlines. Late applications are reviewed only if places remain.

faqs.question: Can the application fee be waived?
faqs.answer: Yes. The $60 application fee is waived for applicants who qualify for a national free or reduced lunch programme, have received a college-board fee waiver, or demonstrate financial hardship. Select the fee waiver option in the application and attach supporting evidence.

faqs.question: What documents are required for my application?
faqs.answer: You need official secondary school transcripts, standardised test scores (optional for most programmes), a personal statement, two recommendation letters, and a copy of your passport or national ID. International applicants must also provide proof of English proficiency.

faqs.question: How can I check the status of my application?
faqs.answer: Sign in to the applicant portal at admissions.northfield.edu and open the 'Application Status' tab. The checklist shows which documents have been received and whether your file is complete or under review. Decisions are posted to the portal and emailed to you.

faqs.question: What English proficiency scores do international students need?
faqs.answer: Undergraduate applicants need a minimum TOEFL iBT score of 80, IELTS Academic 6.5, or Duolingo English Test 110. Graduate programmes require TOEFL 90 or IELTS 7.0. Students who completed their secondary education in English may request an exemption.

faqs.question: How much is tuition and how do I pay my fees?
faqs.answer: Undergraduate tuition is $14,500 per semester for full-time students. Pay online through the Student Finance portal using bank transfer or credit card, or enrol in a monthly instalment plan with a small administration fee. Payment is due two weeks before the semester begins.

faqs.question: What scholarships and financial aid are available?
faqs.answer: Northfield offers merit scholarships of up to 50 percent of tuition, need-based grants, and work-study positions. Submit the financial aid application and scholarship essay by the admission deadline. Aid packages are announced together with admission decisions.

faqs.question: Can I transfer credits from another college?
faqs.answer: Yes. Submit official transcripts and course syllabi from your previous institution. The registrar will evaluate courses completed with a grade of C or higher at accredited institutions, and up to 60 credits may be transferred toward an undergraduate degree.

faqs.question: Can I defer my admission to the next year?
faqs.answer: Admitted students may request a one-year deferral by submitting the Deferral Form and a short statement of your plans before May 1. Pay the enrolment deposit to hold your place. Scholarship offers are reviewed again when you re-enrol.

faqs.question: How do I register for courses or change my schedule?
faqs.answer: Log in to the Student Information System and open 'Course Registration'. Search by subject or course code, add classes to your cart, and submit. You can add or drop courses without penalty during the first two weeks of the semester. Meet your academic advisor if you need a registration hold lifted.

faqs.question: How do I request an official transcript?
faqs.answer: Order transcripts through the Registrar's page in the Student Information System. Electronic transcripts are delivered within one business day for $5, and printed sealed transcripts are mailed within five business days for $10. Holds on your account must be cleared first.

faqs.question: How do I apply for on-campus housing?
faqs.answer: After accepting your admission offer, log in to the Housing Portal and complete the residence application with your room-type preferences and roommate requests. Applications are allocated in order of deposit date, so submit your $300 deposit as soon as possible.
